result.summary: none. Lens: bini_search.py evaluate() fifty-move block (lines 164-183). Checked: RULE50 is a module-level int (line 57, env BINI_RULE50 default '1') so numba freezes it as a compile-time constant; S_HALF is imported from bini_board (line 36) and st is an int64 array (bini_board.py:705), so hm is int64. nnue_eval returns np.int64 (bini_nnue.py:274), calibrate and endgame_scale keep int64, so s*(200-hm) stays int64 with no overflow possible (|s| is a bounded static score; even 30000*200 is ~6e6). Sign handling is symmetric (both branches truncate toward zero; s=0 from endgame_scale stays 0). hm is clamped from above at 100 so a FEN halfmove clock >100 is harmless; a negative hm can only come from a malformed FEN and even then only scales by >1 with no crash. Mate scores never pass through evaluate(); corrected() clamps to +/-(MATE_IN_MAX-1) after it. In search() and qsearch() the st[S_HALF] >= 100 rule-draw/contempt returns run before any evaluate() call at non-root nodes; at the root evaluate() runs with clamped hm. TT (tt_store, line 450) stores search scores only, no static eval, so the hm-dependence introduces path dependence but no crash, illegal move or wrong branch. qsearch stand-pat (line 630) and search static (line 813) consume the int64 result through corrected() as before. No concrete self-loss scenario found in this block.

findings.claim: nnue_refresh_persp's explicit signature hard-codes the accumulator as int16[:, :, ::1], but the accumulator dtype is chosen at import (ACC_DTYPE = int32 when ACC_BOUND = max|B1| + 32*max|W1| >= 32767, or BINI_ACC32=1). bini_search.py already makes its _ACC signature follow ACC_DTYPE; bini_nnue.py does not, so the two are inconsistent for any net whose bound does not fit int16.
findings.failure_scenario: With a shipped nnue.safetensors whose ACC_BOUND >= 32767 (the comment in bini_nnue says the 1024 SCReLU nets do not fit), new_accumulators() returns an int32 3-D array. In agent._build -> E.warm_up -> engine.set_position -> N.nnue_refresh (lazily jitted) the call nnue_refresh_persp(bb, pcs, acc, ply, 0, w1, b1) has acc typed array(int32, 3d, C); the dispatcher has compile disabled (explicit signature) and arrays do not convert across dtypes, so numba raises a TypingError 'No matching definition for argument type(s)'. _build catches it, prints BUILD FAILED, and the python-chess material-only fallback plays the entire game (effectively a lost game against any real opponent). Harmless if the exact shipped net was verified to print 'nnue=on' in the ready line with this build; the ship directory contains no nnue.safetensors so I could not confirm the bound.

result.summary: Lens: the ten explicit numba signatures. Checked every call site across bini_board.py, bini_nnue.py, bini_search.py, bini_engine.py, agent.py (bini_eval.py imports rook_att/bishop_att but never calls them; bini_calib.py calls none). Scalar arguments all type-check: every `sq`/`frm`/`to`/`ksq`/`eksq` comes from lsb() (returns int64 via DEBRUIJN_TABLE), literals, or int64 st[]/pcs[]/ui[] reads; every `occ` is uint64 (bb[14], or SQBB xors in see()); `side`/`them`/`by`/`p`/`which` are int64 from st[S_SIDE], range(), or literals; `captures_only` is a boolean expression (`not (in_chk or quiet_checks)` unifies to boolean); tt_store gets uint64 key = bb[15], int64 best/depth/flag/age/ply (INF=32000 is int; evaluate/calibrate/endgame_scale all return int64). Arrays match declared layouts: bb uint64[16] 1-D C, st/pcs/mv int64 1-D C (new_move_stack is flat 1-D), tt_key uint64/tt_data int64 1-D, w1 int16 2-D C, b1 int32 1-D via ascontiguousarray. Return types match the bodies (attacked returns only True/False; _add/gen_moves/king_id/_feature/corr_index return int64 expressions; tt_store/nnue_refresh_persp return nothing). Python-level callers (Engine.legal_moves, uci_to_move, B.warm_up) pass Python int 0 and bool False plus correctly-typed arrays, so dispatch with compile disabled succeeds. The only concrete risk found: bini_nnue.py:159 hard-codes int16 for the accumulator while ACC_DTYPE can be int32 depending on the net's weight bound (bini_search.py's _ACC is dynamic, bini_nnue's is not); a mismatch would surface as a TypingError in agent._build and demote the whole game to the python-chess fallback. Out-of-lens observation worth a glance: the ship directory ship_bp336_v18 contains no nnue.safetensors, so as-is bini_nnue takes the zero-weights fallback (LOADED=False, nnue=off, HCE-only play) unless the weights file is added at packaging or BINI_NNUE is set.

findings.claim: ship_bp336_v18 contains no nnue.safetensors and no book.json (sibling dirs ship_bp336 and ship_bp336_v11 both have them). bini_nnue falls back silently to LOADED=False / zero weights, Engine sets use_nnue=False, and agent.py's _BOOK stays empty: the frozen build would play classical-eval only, bookless, with no error.
findings.failure_scenario: Freeze/zip this directory as-is: import succeeds, the ready line prints 'nnue=off', every move is searched with bini_eval instead of the net and the book window is dead. build_packages.py (FinalsDay/night_evidence) hard-lists nnue.safetensors and book.json and would raise FileNotFoundError on this dir, so either the package build fails minutes before the deadline or a hand-zip ships the weak engine. Check: the ready line must say nnue=on and a 'book' log line must appear on move 1.

findings.claim: COMPILE_JOIN_S=21 is a join timeout measured from thread start, not from _T_IMPORT, and the work before the thread starts is not 'tables only': bini_board.py compiles gen_moves (lines 290-474), attacked, rook_att, bishop_att and _add EAGERLY at import (explicit @njit signatures, cache=False, NUMBA_OPT=3) on the main thread, after importing numba and building ~100k rook magic entries in pure Python; after the join, gc.collect() runs while the compile thread competes for the GIL. Total import = chess+numba import + tables + eager compile + 21 s + gc, with no cap.
findings.failure_scenario: On a slow single platform core the pre-thread part (numba import ~1 s, magic tables ~1 s, eager gen_moves compile 3-6 s) plus 21 s join plus a 0.5-1 s gc.collect exceeds the 30 s init budget: the harness never sees the ready line and the game is forfeited before move 1. One-line fix: _thread.join(timeout=max(0.0, COMPILE_JOIN_S - (time.perf_counter() - _T_IMPORT))) with COMPILE_JOIN_S ~24, so the join is anchored to import start.

findings.claim: When _build raises (_build_error set, _ready never set) get_move still executes _ready.wait(min(0.35*time_left, 45 s)) on EVERY move, then hands the fallback remaining = min(1.5, (hard - total_elapsed)/1000, ...) where total_elapsed includes the wait, so remaining is usually negative -> 10 ms.
findings.failure_scenario: Build fails on the platform (e.g. numba compile error, unwritable /tmp/numba_cache, weights parse error): move 1 sleeps 42 s, move 2 sleeps 27 s, move 3 18 s ... the clock collapses to a few seconds within 6-8 moves and the python-chess fallback then plays every move at ~20 ms depth 1 for the rest of the game. Not a clock forfeit (the wait is 35% of what is left) but a guaranteed loss where a 1.5 s-per-move fallback could hold. Fix: `if not _ready.is_set() and _build_error is None:`.

findings.claim: The book path and both _state.record_reply calls (lines 268, 319) are outside the try/except: chess.Move.from_uci(bm) raises chess.InvalidMoveError for a malformed book string (wrong length/characters) and entry.get raises AttributeError if a book value is not a dict.
findings.failure_scenario: A corrupt or hand-edited book.json entry such as {"move": "e7e8"} for a promotion or a non-dict value makes get_move raise on that opening move and the game is lost. Only reachable with a malformed book (moot if no book.json ships); wrapping the book lookup in try/except costs nothing.

result.summary: Time-management path itself checks out: _budget keeps hard <= min(2.2*soft, 0.2*tl, tl-1500) with tighter caps under 30 s/10 s/4 s, think() aborts on a perf_counter deadline every 1024/4096 nodes, the wait path re-budgets on the reduced clock and resets t_think, the single-legal-move and no-legal-move cases return before any budgeting, and the fallback deadline is wall-clock bounded; I found no concrete way to exceed time_left. The concrete risks are elsewhere: (1) the v18 directory has no nnue.safetensors and no book.json while its siblings do, so frozen as-is the engine plays nnue=off and bookless (and build_packages.py would fail on it); (2) the 21 s compile join is not anchored to import start while bini_board eagerly compiles gen_moves and friends on the main thread before the thread starts, so the 30 s ready line has an uncapped margin on a slow core; (3) a failed build still costs 35% of the clock per move in _ready.wait before the starved fallback plays; (4) book lookup and record_reply sit outside the try/except (only matters with a malformed book).

result.reason: The factual observation is correct (ship_bp336_v18 in the scratchpad cands dir holds only the 8 .py files; bini_nnue.py:37/74-83 falls back silently to LOADED=False and zero weights when nnue.safetensors is absent next to __file__, bini_engine.py:39 then sets use_nnue=False, agent.py:96-97 leaves _BOOK empty when book.json is absent, and the ready line at agent.py:330 would print nnue=off). But this is not a defect in the code that will be frozen, and it cannot occur under the stated premise 'NNUE on with shipped defaults': the load paths are Path(__file__).parent / 'nnue.safetensors' and / 'book.json', which are exactly where the packaging step places them. build_packages.py (FinalsDay/night_evidence) never reads this scratchpad dir at all: it zips from Path.home()/'chess'/<build> (line 6-7), a directory that does not exist on this Mac, so the packaging runs on the remote box against its own build dirs; whether those contain the assets is unknowable from here, and the sibling code-only dir ship_bp336_v16_test shows the cands/* dirs are conventionally code overlays, with the 12.6 MB net and 13 MB book living in the base ship dirs (ship_bp336, ship_bp336_v11, ship_v85_v13). Since the scenario depends on a packaging omission rather than on any code path, and cannot happen once nnue.safetensors and book.json sit beside agent.py (the shipped default), it is refuted under the given criterion (also: uncertain -> refuted). The one useful residue is the checklist item: after zipping, confirm the ready line says nnue=on and a 'book' log line appears on move 1, and note the fallback is silent (no error is printed for a missing net).

The code reading is accurate (bini_nnue.py:36/75 falls back to LOADED=False and zero weights when nnue.safetensors is absent next to __file__; bini_engine.py:39 then sets use_nnue=False; agent.py:96-99 leaves _BOOK empty without book.json), and the scratchpad dir ship_bp336_v18 does indeed hold only the .py files. But the premise "freeze/zip this directory as-is" does not describe the real ship path. The frozen artifact is submission_V18_bp336_book_c80eg_r50_nocorr_dcp150_mb125_init_fastcompile2.zip (sha256 6ff2ee09...), built by build_packages.py on gcp-x86 "from ~/chess/ship_bp336_v18" and recorded in /Users/architbhardwaj/Desktop/AI Chessathon/FinalsDay/night_evidence/packages_manifest.txt: it lists nnue.safetensors (321bbd11efd7123e) and book.json (13ce997aafa9b7c8), unzipped 25,730,051 B (consistent with the 12.6 MB net + 13.0 MB book), and all eight .py hashes in that manifest match the local ship_bp336_v18 sources byte-for-byte (verified with shasum: agent.py b0ac6204..., bini_nnue.py a275c9f0..., bini_search.py f6298b00..., etc.). The weights and book hashes are identical to the ship_bp336 siblings. So build_packages.py did not raise FileNotFoundError, the package contains the net and book, and the local directory is a source-only mirror of the packaged build, not the thing being zipped. The Cause Table (13:45) also records the exact-zip battery running on that zip and the upload call made. With the shipped package, WEIGHTS_PATH exists, LOADED=True, Engine.use_nnue=True, the ready line prints nnue=on and the book is populated, so the "classical-only, bookless" scenario cannot occur in a real game. Even in the hypothetical, the path is a graceful fallback with no crash, illegal move, or time forfeit.
